claim: Coca-Cola discloses advertising costs inside selling general and administrative expenses
what_it_does_not_establish: Total marketing spend. The company states all other marketing expenditures are expensed separately, and gives no split by brand, market or channel
how_to_use_it: As the ceiling on what a global advertiser admits to spending on advertising alone. Note the same filing restates 2024 from 5.0bn to 5.1bn, so cite the filing as well as the year

claim: P&G discloses advertising costs covering television print radio digital and in-store
source_name: SEC Form 10-K Note 1 Selling General and Administrative Expense
what_it_does_not_establish: Total marketing spend, and the filing says so: consumer promotions, product sampling and sales aids sit outside this line
how_to_use_it: As a floor, never a total. The gap between this figure and real marketing spend is exactly the promotion and sampling money that most decks forget exists

claim: Nike reports a demand creation line covering brand marketing and sports marketing
what_it_does_not_establish: The split between brand marketing and sports marketing. Nike gives only directional commentary, so endorsement money and media money are indistinguishable here
how_to_use_it: As the clearest published definition of what a marketing line contains. Nike also capitalises prepaid demand creation, 1438m USD at year end, which is the only public evidence of marketing money sitting on a balance sheet

claim: Unilever discloses brand and marketing investment as an of-which line inside selling and administrative expenses
what_it_does_not_establish: The media, production and promotional split. Comparatives are also restated for the Ice Cream demerger, so figures from filings before 2025 are not comparable
how_to_use_it: As the widest definition on this list: it includes media, advertising production, promotional materials and consumer engagement, so it is the closest thing to a disclosed total marketing budget

claim: Unilever states brand and marketing investment as a percentage of turnover
what_it_does_not_establish: That the ratio is a target or a rule. It rose 10bp while the absolute euro figure fell, because of currency
how_to_use_it: As the answer to what a serious FMCG advertiser actually spends as a share of revenue, which is far above every survey benchmark in this table. Also note the step-up of 300bp over five years

claim: Marketing budgets as a share of company revenues
scope: Senior US marketing leaders, 97 percent VP or above
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about small businesses or non-US markets, and anything verified. It is what marketing leaders report about their own budgets
how_to_use_it: As one of two benchmarks quoted together, never alone. Sub-questions fall to n=138, and the same report shows small firms much higher: 13.7 percent for firms under 10m USD revenue

claim: Marketing budgets as a share of total company budgets
what_it_does_not_establish: A trend. The series runs 9.8 in Aug-21 up to 13.8 in Sept-22 and back to 9.6 in 2026, which is volatility rather than direction
how_to_use_it: To kill the phrase industry standard. A benchmark that swings four points in four years is a distribution, not a standard

claim: Marketing budgets as a share of company revenue in a large-enterprise sample
scope: CMOs and marketing leaders, vast majority above 1bn USD revenue, North America UK and Europe
what_it_does_not_establish: The spread. Gartner publishes a mean with no distribution, and gartner.com returns 403 to anything but a browser
how_to_use_it: Alongside the CMO Survey figure to show the gap. 7.8 against 9.0 is two samples asking differently, which is the honest headline: any percent-of-revenue benchmark carries about 1.5 points of sampling slack

claim: Acquisition budgets exceed retention budgets
what_it_does_not_establish: That the split is correct. The same report has 43.7 percent naming loyalty and retention as their main response to economic uncertainty
how_to_use_it: To name a contradiction out loud in a plan review. 82.0 percent of firms spend more on acquisition than retention while saying retention is the priority, and the gap has widened from 14.7 percent in 2022

claim: Share of digital marketing activity performed by external agencies and partners
what_it_does_not_establish: Which activities. A third of the work being outside says nothing about whether the strategy or the execution left the building
how_to_use_it: As the baseline when someone claims in-housing has won. It has moved from 31.6 percent in 2022 to 33.6 percent, in the opposite direction, and Retail and CPG outsource over half

claim: Social media as a share of marketing budget
what_it_does_not_establish: The forecast. Respondents predict 17.1 percent in a year and 23.1 percent in five
how_to_use_it: As a lesson in reading forecasts. The report notes its own twelve-month social projections have overshot actuals by an average of 2.1 points, which is the rare case of a survey grading itself

claim: Self-rated ability to demonstrate marketing ROI from martech
what_it_does_not_establish: A precise value. The report's narrative says 4.2 where its table pairs 4.4, so it disagrees with itself
how_to_use_it: As evidence that attribution is unsolved at firms far better resourced than your client. No martech capability in the battery scores above 5, and hiring to manage martech scores 3.7

claim: Mean short-term advertising elasticity
source_name: Sethuraman, Tellis and Briesch, Journal of Marketing Research
what_it_does_not_establish: That your advertising has this elasticity. It is a mean across five decades that varies by durability, life-cycle stage, data frequency and whether advertising was measured in GRPs or money
how_to_use_it: As the strongest available caution against planning constants. The prior accepted mean from the same literature was 0.22, nearly double, which means a widely used benchmark was wrong by 100 percent for years

claim: Mean long-term advertising elasticity
source_name: Sethuraman, Tellis and Briesch, Journal of Marketing Research
what_it_does_not_establish: ROI. An elasticity says nothing without margin and current spend level, and the paper reports elasticity declining over time
how_to_use_it: To size an expectation before a test. Doubling spend on this mean moves volume by roughly a sixth, which is the number a client needs before approving a budget, not after

claim: The brand-building to activation budget split attributed to Binet and Field
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything. The ratio appears on no free IPA page; searching the full text of both report landing pages for the figure returns nothing, and the reports are paid
how_to_use_it: As the worked example of a number everyone repeats and nobody opened. When you do cite it, state that it is an average across self-selected effectiveness-award entries, so the sample is campaigns that won prizes and it cannot tell one brand which side of the average it is on

claim: Share of business buyers not in the market at any one time
scope: B2B categories with long repurchase cycles
what_it_does_not_establish: A rule, and the author says so in the article: the figure is a heuristic to get the idea across. The five-year repurchase cycle it derives from is asserted, not sourced
how_to_use_it: As an argument for reach over in-market targeting, with the disclaimer quoted. It is wrong for fast-cycle categories, so derive your own figure from your own purchase cycle before using it

claim: Smaller brands have both fewer buyers and less loyal buyers
sample: a range of empirical evidence, not quantified in the abstract
source_name: Ehrenberg, Goodhardt and Barwise, Journal of Marketing
what_it_does_not_establish: Universality. The authors' own abstract covers known exceptions and deviations, and the institute publishes on deviations such as the iPhone
how_to_use_it: To stop a client chasing loyalty as a growth route while penetration is flat. Then look for the exception, because a brand that violates double jeopardy is the interesting case and the law tells you to check

claim: Brand salience is propensity to be noticed or come to mind in buying situations and is not awareness
what_it_does_not_establish: Any effect size. The paper argues salience is not awareness and does not quantify how much mental availability moves share
how_to_use_it: To reject an awareness percentage as a brand metric. Ask instead how many buying situations the brand comes to mind in, which is a different and harder question

claim: Targeting heavy buyers is a misconception because they are hard to nudge higher
what_it_does_not_establish: The statistic everyone attaches to it. The page contains no Pareto share; the buyer-frequency distributions are in the paid books
how_to_use_it: As the argument, without the number. If you need the volume share of light buyers, buy the book or measure your own base, because the open web does not carry it

claim: Vietnam ecommerce gross merchandise value
source_name: Google, Temasek and Bain e-Conomy SEA
what_it_does_not_establish: Net revenue or any individual business. It is GMV, gross of the high Vietnamese cash-on-delivery return rate, and Bain analysis rather than measurement
how_to_use_it: With its scope stated. Total digital economy is 39bn USD of which ecommerce 25bn, transport and food 5bn, travel 4bn, media 6bn

claim: Vietnam ecommerce revenue and growth
sample: thousands of businesses surveyed with provincial support; exact n not published
what_it_does_not_establish: Agreement with e-Conomy SEA. Two credible sources, two definitions, seven months apart
how_to_use_it: Next to the 25bn figure, never averaged with it. The more useful finding is that 21 percent is the lowest growth rate of the past decade, and that the 2026 edition reports provinces cut from 63 to 34, which makes every province-level benchmark built before 2026 stale

claim: Average order value in Vietnamese video commerce
source_name: Google, Temasek and Bain e-Conomy SEA
what_it_does_not_establish: Margin. An order value is not a contribution, and marketplace fees rose again in 2026
how_to_use_it: As the hard ceiling on Vietnamese live-selling acquisition cost. At 6 USD an order, any tactic costing more than about a dollar to produce an order is underwater before goods cost. Seller count and transaction volume both grew 60 percent, in lockstep, so there is no per-seller productivity gain to bank on

claim: Facebook reported advertising reach in Vietnam
source_name: DataReportal, We Are Social and Meltwater
what_it_does_not_establish: People. This is addressable ad accounts including duplicates, dormant accounts and bots, and it exceeds the adult population
how_to_use_it: Only as a relative figure. Never divide it by an NSO population count and call the result penetration. The same report shows TikTok reach falling 39.7 percent year on year, which is a platform restating its own planner methodology, not usage declining

claim: Zalo Official Account Standard tier annual price
what_it_does_not_establish: Delivery or open rates, and whether an account qualifies. List prices change without notice
how_to_use_it: To cost a Zalo plan honestly for a household or small business, which is the tier the page itself positions for hokinhdoanh

claim: Free broadcast messages per follower per month on Zalo Official Account
figure: 4 on Growth and Comprehensive tiers only
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether anyone reads them. Zalo also enforces a 48-hour service window, meters replies outside it, and forbids messaging users who have never interacted
how_to_use_it: To kill a broadcast-based Zalo plan before it is sold. Basic and Standard tiers get zero free broadcasts, so the plan a small shop can afford cannot broadcast at all, which invalidates most published Zalo playbooks

claim: Zalo template message price per send
what_it_does_not_establish: The response rate. A send price is a cost line and not a channel evaluation
how_to_use_it: To compute a per-order messaging cost against a 6 USD average order value. Authentication payment and voucher templates cost 300 VND, other templates 200, the first call-to-action button is free and each additional one costs 100

claim: Average documented cart abandonment rate
what_it_does_not_establish: Marketplace funnels or Vietnam. An in-app Shopee or TikTok Shop checkout is not a cart, and the studies use different definitions
how_to_use_it: As roughly seven in ten, never as 70.22. The usable part is the mechanics beside it: US checkouts average 23 form fields and a benchmark of 60 leading sites averaged 39 improvable checkout areas

claim: Amazon replaces slide presentations with narratively structured six-page memos read silently at the start of a meeting
what_it_does_not_establish: Any template, and anything about marketing. It is an essay about high standards
how_to_use_it: As the corrective to the popular six-page PR-slash-FAQ. Amazon's own pages describe a six-page meeting memo and a one-page press release as two different documents

claim: Amazon writes a one-page press release and an FAQ before requesting budget or writing code
figure: 1 page press release plus separate FAQ
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether it works outside Amazon, or when it was written. The page carries no date of any kind
how_to_use_it: As the most transferable artefact in this table. The FAQ has two halves, customer questions first and internal questions second, and the internal half is where cannibalisation and resourcing get asked before the money is spent

claim: P&G states it invented brand management in 1931 to create a single point of accountability for the brands at the centre of the business model
what_it_does_not_establish: That a brand manager holds a profit and loss. P&G's own FY2025 10-K puts direct profit responsibility at Sector Business Unit level, not brand level, and no P&G-published one-page brand strategy template could be found
how_to_use_it: As the origin of the general-manager framing, with the 10-K correction attached. The transferable part is the three named brand disciplines: consumer and market knowledge, communications, and design

claim: Coca-Cola describes a category-led geography-executed marketing structure with a shared platform-services organisation
what_it_does_not_establish: Headcount, agency arrangements, in-housing, or how brand and performance budgets are governed
how_to_use_it: As the rare primary description of a marketing operating model. Operating units execute locally, global marketing category leadership teams own the category, and a platform services organisation supplies consumer analytics, digital commerce and social hubs as a shared service
